answer_1.quote: We adopt multi-task learning and make conversational models learn the skills simultaneously. By expressing, explaining, and revising moral views in dialogue exchanges, conversational models learn morality well in a natural manner.
answer_1.outputs: dialogue responses (answers, explanations, revisions, inferred RoTs)

answer_2.quote: We propose a reference-free method to evaluate the ability of answering, explanation, revision and inference under our framework based on dynamic interacting. This method primarily learns a trainable metric to measure the agreement between an answer and a RoT given a question.

answer_4.quote: We conduct human interactive experiments to verify that (1) our proposed metrics ... (2) ... We let the crowd-workers interact with models in real-time and do not limit moral topics and dialogue flows. Meanwhile, for each sentence generated by conversational models, the crowdworkers are asked to annotate (1) whether the sentence embodies morality (Embodiment, 1: yes, 0: no), (2) if it does, how much proportion of people would accept the moral standpoint (Morality, from 1: none to 5: all). Following, we also evaluate Sensibleness and Specificity of each sentence, which measures the general dialogue ability (1: yes, 0: no).
answer_4.guideline: Annotators label Embodiment of morality, rate Morality proportion, and assess Sensibleness and Specificity of each generated sentence.
